title: PolarAlignmentNode cannot be added to a sequence - it is absent from the palette
summary: Confirmed real and objectively wrong: PolarAlignmentNode has a model (alignment_and_dome.dart:319), a properties editor (_motion_rich.dart:978), serialisation on both the file and repository paths, a time estimate, validation coverage, a registered Rust executor (native/skotiq_native/sequencer/src/node/registry.rs:114) and is emitted by SmartNightService - but no palette entry existed in any category, so the only way to get one into a sequence was to have Smart Night generate it or to hand-edit a file. Added a 'Polar Alignment' item to the Mount category next to Meridian Flip. Its isNorth follows the observer latitude the same way SmartNightService derives it (sequence_emitter.dart:310), so a southern-hemisphere operator does not silently get a node that rotates about the north celestial pole.
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/node_palette_polar_alignment_test.dart - 4 cases: the item exists under Mount and creates a PolarAlignmentNode; a search for 'polar' over name+description is non-empty (the exact repro from the finding); latitude -33.9 yields isNorth false; latitude +41.5 yields isNorth true. 4/4 pass.
revert_check: Deleted the whole NodePaletteItem block added at node_palette.dart:320-333 (the 'Polar Alignment' entry). All 4 tests failed. Restored from a byte copy; 4/4 pass again.

title: Palette search with no matches renders a completely blank panel
summary: Confirmed. Every palette surface fed rankNodePaletteMatches straight into a ListView.builder, so an empty result rendered zero children and the body went blank between the search field and the help tip - indistinguishable from a failed load. There are THREE such surfaces, not one: the toolbox Nodes tab (sequencer_screen_parts/node_palette.dart), and both branches of the standalone NodePalette (desktop sidebar + mobile add-node sheet). Added a shared NodePaletteEmptyState that names the query back ('No nodes match "polar"'), says what to try, and carries a working Clear search button; wired into all three.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/node_palette_empty_state_test.dart - 3 cases, one per surface. The toolbox case drives the real SequencerScreen, types a no-match term into 'Search nodes...', asserts the empty state and its exact message render, then taps 'Clear search' and asserts the catalogue comes back (the Imaging header reappears) - so the affordance is proven live, not just present. 3/3 pass.
revert_check: Forced the ListView branch at all three call sites (`filteredCategories.isEmpty` -> `false && filteredCategories.isEmpty` in widgets/node_palette.dart:185 and :350 and sequencer_screen_parts/node_palette.dart:111). All 3 tests failed. Restored from byte copies; 3/3 pass.

title: Validation badges on the sequence header are not clickable, so the only way to read '1 error' is to press Start
summary: Confirmed: _ValidationBadges rendered plain Containers with no gesture handler, the Builder has no issues panel, and the only route to the issue text was the pre-flight dialog - i.e. pressing the button that arms the rig. Badges are now an InkWell ('Show sequence issues') opening a read-only SequenceIssuesDialog that lists the live validation issues errors-first with title, description and resolution hint, and selects the offending node when an issue names one. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: the finding's second half, reclassifying 'Empty Sequence'/'No Exposures' from error to info. Those two genuinely block Start, so error is the honest severity; softening it would make the badge lie in the other direction. The real complaint - that you could not read what the badge meant - is what is fixed.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/validation_badge_opens_issues_test.dart - drives the real SequenceTree with a target still carrying the (0h,+0deg) placeholder, waits out the 500 ms live-validation debounce, then reads liveValidationProvider and requires the dialog to render EVERY issue the badge counted (not hard-coded rule text), and that tapping an issue with an affectedNodeId closes the dialog and sets selectedNodeIdProvider to that node. 1 case, passes.
revert_check: Replaced the Tooltip+InkWell wrapper in support_widgets.dart:611 with Builder+IgnorePointer (the pre-fix inert badge). The test failed. Restored from a byte copy; passes.

title: Live Stacking's explanatory helper text is truncated to one ellipsised line
summary: Confirmed, and the cause is not in that file. Flutter's InputDecoration.helperMaxLines defaults to null, which its own docs define as 'soft line breaks are truncated with an ellipse' - the helper Text is built with overflow: TextOverflow.ellipsis and maxLines: helperMaxLines (input_decorator.dart:397-402). Nothing in the app ever set it, so EVERY helperText in the app ellipsised, not just these two. Set helperMaxLines: 4 once in SkotiqTheme's inputDecorationTheme, which is the single factory behind dark/light/redNight/accent themes. All 15 helperText call sites in the repo live in scrolling property panels or dialogs, so wrapping costs nothing and no layout is forced taller than its container.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/live_stacking_helper_wrap_test.dart - 2 cases against the real LiveStackingProperties in a 360 px panel. First asserts the rendered helper Text for BOTH sentences from the finding has maxLines > 1. Second reaches the RenderParagraph and asserts didExceedMaxLines is false and the laid-out height exceeds one line height - i.e. it actually wrapped rather than merely being allowed to. 2/2 pass.
revert_check: Deleted the `helperMaxLines: 4,` line from skotiq_theme.dart:230. Both tests failed. Restored from a byte copy; 2/2 pass.
caveats: Incidental, out of scope, NOT fixed: DropdownButtonFormField in live_stacking_properties.dart:179 overflows its row by 8 px when the panel is 300 px wide. The properties panel's own minimum width is 270 px, so this is reachable on a 1024-wide window. Not one of the findings; flagged for a later pass.

title: Two different things are called Save, two different things are called Templates, and the tab names collide
summary: Both halves confirmed. (1) The toolbar floppy was labelled 'Save Sequence' and calls SequenceFileService.exportSequence - an OS file chooser writing a .nsq - while the Sequences tab's 'Save Current' is what persists into the app. Relabelled to 'Export Sequence File...' (and the force-save dialog's operationName with it). (2) The Builder's left panel is the 'Snippets' tab, its import tooltip already said 'Import snippet from file...', it stores TemplateSnippets - and it titled itself 'Templates', the name of a top-level tab holding whole saved sequences. The panel now says 'Snippets' in both its wide and compact headers, searches 'Search snippets...', and its help/tooltip copy says snippet. This is a self-contradiction inside one panel, not a taste call.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/naming_collisions_test.dart - 2 cases: the real SequenceToolbar exposes tooltip 'Export Sequence File...' and no longer 'Save Sequence'; the real SnippetPalette renders 'Snippets' and renders no 'Templates' text or 'Search templates...' field. 2/2 pass.
revert_check: Restored 'Save Sequence' in sequence_toolbar.dart:518-519 and 'Templates'/'Search templates...' in snippet_palette/rendering.dart:45,160,325. Both tests failed. Restored from byte copies; 2/2 pass.

title: Filter is a free-text field with no binding to the wheel; a typo becomes a 2am run failure
summary: Half of this was already true in the tree and half was a real gap. NOT real: 'Change Filter's Properties offers a plain text box' - _FilterChangeProperties (_capture_rich.dart:103-160) renders a DropdownButton over the ACTIVE PROFILE's filterNames, falls back to free text only when the profile declares none, and already surfaces a stored-but-missing name as an explicit '(not in profile)' row plus a warning. REAL: 'validate the name against the profile at build time rather than at run time'. FilterInWheelRule only runs when a filter wheel is CONNECTED (filter_rules.dart:43-46), which is never true while a sequence is built in daylight - so 'Ha' vs 'H-alpha' survived the builder. Added FilterInProfileRule: when no wheel is connected and the active profile declares filters, every enabled ExposureNode.filter and FilterChangeNode.filterName must match one (case-insensitively) or it warns, naming the node. Silent when the profile lists nothing (nothing to check against) and silent when a wheel is connected (the live wheel is the better authority). Refactored the shared node walk into one _filterUses helper so the two rules cannot drift.
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/rules/filter_in_profile_rule_test.dart - 7 cases: a mismatched FilterChangeNode warns and names the node; a mismatched ExposureNode warns; a case-insensitive match is silent; an empty profile filter list is silent (cry-wolf guard); no active profile is silent; a CONNECTED wheel that really carries the name is silent even though the profile is stale (the other cry-wolf direction); a disabled node is ignored. 7/7 pass. Full skotiq_core test/providers/sequence suite re-run: 513/513 pass, so the new rule does not disturb existing issue counts.
revert_check: Replaced FilterInProfileRule's issue-building return with `return const [];` in filter_rules.dart:120. The two warn cases failed, the five silence cases still passed - i.e. the test discriminates the behaviour, not the file. Restored from a byte copy; 7/7 pass.

title: Loop defaults to 1 iteration and Conditional defaults to 'Always Execute' - both are no-ops out of the box
summary: Confirmed: the palette builds LoopNode() (conditionType count, repeatCount 1) and ConditionalNode() (conditionType always), so both nodes arrive doing exactly nothing and the tree shows no sign of it. Added NoOpLogicNodeRule, which flags a count-type Loop at <= 1 iteration and a Conditional set to Always, at INFO severity, with affectedNodeId set so the tree paints the node and the header badge counts it - and, thanks to the badge fix in this same batch, the operator can now read it in one click. I deliberately did NOT invent a better default count: 2? 10? is unknowable from here, and picking one would silently impose taste on every sequence built from the palette while ALSO not fixing Conditional (which has no 'unset' value in its enum at all). Surfacing the no-op at build time is the fix that is available without deciding what the operator meant. If the owner wants a non-1 default, that is a one-line follow-up in node_palette.dart.
test: packages/skotiq_core/test/providers/sequence/rules/no_op_logic_node_rule_test.dart - 7 cases. Two of them assert the palette's exact construction (LoopNode() really is count/1, ConditionalNode() really is always) BEFORE asserting the flag, so the test also pins the defaults the finding is about. Plus: a configured Loop is silent, a whileDark loop is left to the existing termination rules, a configured Conditional is silent, a disabled node is ignored, and validateSequence() (the default rule set) surfaces the issue - proving it is registered, not just written. 7/7 pass.
revert_check: Two separate reverts. (a) Removed NoOpLogicNodeRule() from defaultSequenceValidators in sequence_validation.dart:321 -> the 'wired into the default validator set' case failed. (b) Restored that and instead short-circuited the rule body with `if (sequence.nodes.isNotEmpty) return const [];` at logic_node_rules.dart:395 -> the two flag cases and the wiring case failed (3 of 7). Restored from byte copies after each; 7/7 pass, and the whole rules/ directory passes 76/76.

title: No move up / move down in the node context menu - reordering is drag-only
summary: Not real against the current tree, and the second half was never real. Move Up / Move Down entries exist in sequence_tree_context_menu.dart:244-255, sitting between Insert Above/Below and Duplicate, each gated by a computed sibling index with an explanatory disabled tooltip ('Already the first node in its container.'). They are NOT in HEAD (`git show HEAD:...| grep -c moveUp` returns 0) - an earlier uncommitted wave of this campaign added them, which is why the finding, taken against the shipped build, saw drag-only reordering. They are covered by three existing cases in sequence_tree_context_menu_test.dart:358-427, all passing (13/13 in that file). The Group-action asymmetry the finding calls unexplained IS explained, and was already in HEAD: parallelGroupDisabledReason (line 190) carries the tooltip 'Select 2+ adjacent nodes to group in parallel.', because wrapping one node in a Parallel container is semantically a no-op while a Sequential container of one is still a labelled group.
test: No new test. packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/sequence_tree_context_menu_test.dart already covers it: 'Move Up shifts the node one slot earlier among its siblings', 'Move Down shifts the node one slot later among its siblings', 'Move Up is disabled on the first sibling and changes nothing'. Re-run: 13/13 pass.
revert_check: n/a - nothing changed. The finding's remaining ask, an Alt+Up/Alt+Down accelerator, is genuinely absent: kSequenceTreeShortcuts binds bare Up/Down to MOVING THE SELECTION, not the node, so adding reorder accelerators is additive work rather than a defect fix. Left open.

title: Mosaic preview shows only 5 of 9 panel numbers for a 3x3 grid and hides the centre panel's number under the drag handle
summary: Half confirmed, half not reproducible. NOT REPRODUCIBLE: 'only 5 of 9 numbers render'. A widget test over the real MosaicWizardDialog at the default 3x3 grid finds all nine numbers, 1-9, inside the planner - so the missing ones in the screenshot were low-contrast reading, not absent widgets. CONFIRMED and structural: the drag-centre handle is drawn at exactly centerPx (visual_planner.dart:291-305) and every panel number was Center()-ed in its cell, so the middle panel of ANY odd grid had its number under an opaque 12 px accent dot - it can never have been legible. Moved the number to the panel's top-left corner as a small badge with its own scrim: it clears the handle for every grid parity, and the scrim keeps it readable over the neighbouring panels' translucent overlap fills. Added a ValueKey to the handle so the geometry is assertable.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/widgets/mosaic_panel_labels_test.dart - 3 cases on the real dialog with a real optical config. (1) each of the numbers 1..9 is present exactly once inside the keyed planner - this is the case that DISPROVES the 5-of-9 claim, and it passes both before and after, reported honestly. (2) the rendered rect of every number and of the keyed centre handle do not overlap. (3) after clamping the zoom control to its 25% minimum (the smallest panels the planner can draw) there is no layout exception and all nine badges still render - the guard against the new badge overflowing a tiny cell. 3/3 pass; the pre-existing mosaic_wizard_visual_test.dart still passes 7/7.
revert_check: Restored the centred Text (Center + Text('${p.index + 1}')) in visual_planner.dart:352. The overlap case failed ('panel 5's number is under the drag-centre handle'); the all-nine-present case still passed, which is exactly the discrimination described above. Restored from a byte copy; 2/2 pass.

title: Quick-Start Wizard shows both a per-filter Count and a Loop Iterations field and never states the resulting frame total
summary: Real, and worse than reported: the per-filter Count is not merely ambiguous, it is INERT. quick_start_wizard_dialog.dart:794 builds every exposure with `count: 1, // 1 per loop iteration; loop controls total count`, and the time estimator agrees (_estimatedTotalSecs sums ONE frame per enabled filter and multiplies by _loopCount). So the built sequence and its duration estimate are driven entirely by Loop Iterations. Meanwhile _FilterExposureConfig.count is displayed in two places - the step-2 table and the step-5 review row ('${f.count}x ${f.exposureSecs}s', _review_step.dart:51) - and folded into the saved sequence description (_buildDescription, :1143). The preset code deliberately computes DIFFERENT per-filter counts (Ha/OIII x1.5, OSC x2, quick_start_wizard_dialog.dart:613-618, with a comment explaining the weighting) and every one of those weights is then discarded. Result: pick the Ha/OIII preset and the wizard tells you 15 frames per filter while building 10. The finding's 'no total time' half is wrong - an Estimated Duration card exists at _review_step.dart:136-157 - but there is no total FRAME count anywhere. I did not implement a fix: which knob wins decides how many frames every wizard-built night captures, and either answer changes the product.
options: (A) Make Count real as frames-per-filter-per-loop-pass: exposure count := filterConfig.count, total per filter = count x iterations. Both controls then mean something and the displayed per-filter numbers become true, but today's defaults (count 10, iterations 10) would build 100 frames per filter where they build 10 - a 10x change for anyone who has used the wizard before. (B) Delete the per-filter Count column and keep Loop Iterations as the single knob, relabelled 'frames per filter'. Zero change to any built sequence or to the duration estimate, the review step becomes true by construction, and the finding's own suggestion; the cost is that the presets can no longer weight filters differently, which is intent the code currently writes down and then throws away.
recommendation: B, plus a 'N frames, H h M m integration' line on step 2 and step 5. It is the only option that cannot silently change what an existing user's wizard produces tonight, and it makes the wizard self-consistent with the two things that already agree (the builder and the estimator). If the owner wants the preset weighting to be real, that is option A and it should ship with a visible total and a note that frame counts have changed.

title: Building the standard night by hand takes ~21 actions before configuring anything, and the empty Builder points at none of the faster paths
summary: The facts check out. An empty container renders one italic line and nothing else - node_tree_view.dart:471-487, 'Drop instructions here' on desktop / 'Tap + to add instructions' on mobile - with no reference to the Quick-Start Wizard (a toolbar icon) or the Starters (a different top-level tab). Both faster paths exist and are good; neither is visible from the surface a new user lands on. But what the empty canvas should offer is a decision about which workflow the product leads with, and that is squarely the owner's call: it changes the Sequencer's front door, and 'wizard first' vs 'blank canvas first' is the difference between an ASIAIR-style guided app and a NINA-style builder. Not implemented.
options: (A) Turn the empty canvas into a three-way chooser - 'Start from a wizard / Start from a starter / Build manually' - keeping the drop zone underneath. Fastest path to a working night for a first-time user; risks feeling like a nag to the experienced operator who opens the Builder precisely because they intend to build, and it puts a decision in front of every New Sequence. (B) Leave the canvas as a canvas and add one quiet line under the hint - 'or start from the Quick-Start Wizard / a Starter' as inline links. Discoverable without changing what the screen is for; less of a lift for a beginner than (A).
recommendation: B. It closes the actual gap the finding measured (the faster paths are invisible from the place you start) at a fraction of the risk, and it does not commit the product to being wizard-led. Worth pairing with the finding's second ask - an insert-after-selected keyboard entry - which is additive and would cut the 21-action count regardless of which option is chosen.

title: Starters tab says 'copy one into your current sequence' but the action replaces the whole sequence
summary: Confirmed - the app stating something untrue. _useStarter calls CurrentSequenceNotifier.loadSequence, which replaces the loaded sequence outright (it only pauses to confirm when the current one is dirty). 'Copy into' is the one reading that would make an operator tap it with work already loaded. The caption now reads 'Bundled, ready-to-run sample sequences. Loading one replaces your current sequence.' and the button reads 'Replace with this starter'.
test: packages/skotiq_app/test/screens/sequencer/starters_caption_truth_test.dart - 2 cases. One asserts the old promise is gone, the new one is present, and the button carries the new label. The other taps the button on a saved sequence and asserts the editor's sequence is REPLACED (new id, name 'Safe Starter'), so the wording is pinned to behaviour rather than to itself. The existing templates_catalog_test.dart was updated for the new label; both files pass, 6/6.
revert_check: Restored the original subtitle and the 'Use this starter' label in _starters_section.dart:53-59 and :215. Both new tests failed. Restored from a byte copy; 6/6 pass across both files.
